plans.label: Lesson 01
plans.title: Observe with the senses
plans.objective: Record three observations and name the sense used for each.
plans.materials: Leaves, an opaque sound tube, trays and observation cards.

phases.teacher: Show a leaf and ask which features can be checked without guessing.
phases.pupils: Name one feature and say which sense can check it.

phases.teacher: Set up looking, touching and quiet listening stations. Model the difference between “rough” and “looks old”.
phases.pupils: Examine the safe items and record an observation and sense at each station.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to submit three evidence statements and check the sense named for each.
phases.pupils: Submit three observations and identify sight, touch or hearing beside each.

phases.teacher: Ask how two pupils can check a disputed observation.
phases.pupils: Repeat it using the named sense and report what was observed.

plans.follow_up: Separate observable details from opinions.

plans.label: Lesson 02
plans.title: Classify living things
plans.objective: Sort six pictures by one visible feature and state the sorting rule.
plans.materials: Six picture cards of living things and two sorting mats.

phases.teacher: Show a bird and a fish. Ask for one feature that can be seen in both images.
phases.pupils: Suggest a feature such as legs, fins or a visible covering.

phases.teacher: Give pairs six animal pictures with clear features. Ask them to name one testable rule and keep it throughout their sort.
phases.pupils: Place all six cards into two groups using the named visible feature.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil an unsorted copy and check all six placements against their rule.
phases.pupils: Sort the six pictures independently and write the sorting rule.

phases.teacher: Show a new example and ask where it would go.
phases.pupils: Place it using the same feature and explain why.

plans.follow_up: Check pupils use one visible feature throughout.

plans.label: Lesson 03
plans.title: Measure and record length
plans.objective: Select a ruler, measure two objects from the zero mark and record each reading in centimetres.
plans.materials: Centimetre rulers, pencils, strips of card and recording slips.

phases.teacher: Hold a strip at the ruler’s 1 cm mark. Ask where its end should start.
phases.pupils: Identify the zero mark as the starting point.

phases.teacher: Model alignment and show how to read the other end in cm. Give each pair two short objects.
phases.pupils: Take turns aligning each object at zero, reading the scale and recording the length.

phases.teacher: Observe each pupil measuring one of the two objects and check both readings and units on the slip.
phases.pupils: Measure independently, then submit both lengths in centimetres.

phases.teacher: Show a ruler with a gap before the zero mark.
phases.pupils: Explain why the ruler’s edge is different from its zero mark.

plans.follow_up: Reteach alignment at zero and use of cm.

plans.label: Lesson 04
plans.title: Make an inference
plans.objective: State one observation and use it to support one plausible explanation.
plans.materials: Illustrated footprints, comparison cards and an observation–inference sheet.

phases.teacher: Show a picture of damp footprints beside a tap. Ask what the picture actually shows.
phases.pupils: Describe one visible detail without suggesting a cause.

phases.teacher: Model separate observation and inference columns. Give groups two illustrated scenes with more than one possible explanation.
phases.pupils: Record visible clues, suggest an explanation for each scene and compare which clues support it.

phases.teacher: Give an unfamiliar scene to each pupil. Check that the inference is plausible and linked to a visible detail.
phases.pupils: Write one observation and one possible explanation connected by “because”.

phases.teacher: Ask for another explanation that fits the same visible evidence.
phases.pupils: Offer an alternative and say what could be checked next.

plans.follow_up: Check inference is supported by a stated observation.

plans.label: Lesson 05
plans.title: Predict from evidence
plans.objective: Make a prediction and cite a pattern or an earlier observation to support it.
plans.materials: Three picture cards from a growing pattern, a ruler and prediction slips.

phases.teacher: Show three pictures of the same shoot taken on different days.
phases.pupils: Describe the pattern across the three pictures.

phases.teacher: Model using the first two pictures to predict the third. Offer a second sequence with its last picture covered.
phases.pupils: Record a prediction and point to a previous result that supports it.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to finish a prediction sentence and give a reason drawn from the sequence.
phases.pupils: Submit a likely next result with one stated pattern or earlier observation.

phases.teacher: Reveal the covered result and discuss predictions supported by the pattern.
phases.pupils: Compare the result with the prediction and say what evidence was used.

plans.follow_up: Check each prediction includes a previous observation.

plans.label: Lesson 06
plans.title: Communicate findings
plans.objective: Present three observations in a labelled table or drawing and explain one finding.
plans.materials: Shell or leaf cards, magnifiers, paper and sample table headings.

phases.teacher: Show an unlabelled recording sheet and ask what a reader needs to identify each result.
phases.pupils: Suggest a heading, label or key.

phases.teacher: Model two formats using a different specimen. Give groups specimens or clear photographs and ask them to choose a table or drawing.
phases.pupils: Observe three features, record each feature clearly and agree which result to explain.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil’s three observations and ask them to explain one without relying on their partner.
phases.pupils: Submit a labelled table or drawing and explain one recorded finding.

phases.teacher: Compare two recordings that present the same idea differently.
phases.pupils: Identify one label that helped the reader understand a result.

plans.follow_up: Check that labels make all three observations interpretable.

plans.label: Lesson 07
plans.title: Use apparatus and handle specimens
plans.objective: Demonstrate safe use of two tools and transfer a specimen without damaging it.
plans.materials: Magnifiers, blunt tongs, soft brushes, trays and dry leaves.

phases.teacher: Compare a crushed paper leaf with an intact one and ask how tools could protect it.
phases.pupils: Name a way to hold or move a specimen gently.

phases.teacher: Demonstrate proper handling of a magnifier and blunt tongs. Set up labelled practice stations with a specimen transfer path.
phases.pupils: Inspect a specimen using the magnifier and transfer the specimen between trays without crushing it.

phases.teacher: Use a three-point checklist for two tools and the specimen transfer. Rotate so each pupil demonstrates independently.
phases.pupils: Select and use both tools safely, then show the leaf remains intact in the receiving tray.

phases.teacher: Ask what to do if a fragile part breaks or spills.
phases.pupils: Explain how to stop, report and continue after guidance.

plans.follow_up: Recheck grip and handling with fragile specimens.

plans.label: Lesson 08
plans.title: Sketch, clean and store
plans.objective: Draw and label a specimen, clean used apparatus and return it to the correct place.
plans.materials: Specimens, pencils, trays, cleaning cloths, magnifiers and a storage chart.

phases.teacher: Display a sketch with an unclear label and a tray with equipment in the wrong place.
phases.pupils: Suggest one correction to the picture or storage arrangement.

phases.teacher: Model a clear outline and straight label lines. Demonstrate wiping, drying and returning the apparatus after use.
phases.pupils: Observe a specimen, make a labelled sketch, clean the apparatus and match it to its storage place.

phases.teacher: Check every pupil’s drawing and observe each pupil cleaning and storing one item.
phases.pupils: Show a recognisable sketch with labels and demonstrate the correct clean-and-store sequence.

phases.teacher: Ask why damp apparatus is dried before being stored.
phases.pupils: Explain one consequence of putting it away wet.

plans.follow_up: Check sketch labels, cleaning and correct storage separately.

plans.label: Lesson 09
plans.title: Follow science room rules
plans.objective: Demonstrate one rule before, during and after a science room activity and explain one consequence.
plans.materials: Science room rules cards, teacher-made scenario cards and empty apparatus trays.

phases.teacher: Show a picture of a crowded doorway and ask how the class should enter safely.
phases.pupils: State one action that keeps the entrance clear.

phases.teacher: Set up a short dry-run with empty trays and rules cards for before, during and after work.
phases.pupils: Rehearse entering, handling and returning materials safely. Explain each chosen rule to a partner.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil three situation prompts and use a checklist for the three stages and a consequence.
phases.pupils: Demonstrate an appropriate rule at each stage and explain what could happen if one is ignored.

phases.teacher: Ask which rule helps keep the next class safe.
phases.pupils: Name a rule and connect it to a possible consequence.

plans.follow_up: Rehearse the stage pupils overlooked.

plans.label: Lesson 10
plans.title: Types of teeth and functions
plans.objective: Match incisors, canines and molars with cutting, tearing and grinding.
plans.materials: Tooth model or images, shape cards and job labels.

phases.teacher: Show a pointed and a broad tooth and ask what differences are visible.
phases.pupils: Describe the two shapes and propose a job for each.

phases.teacher: Point to incisors, canines and molars on an image. Use cards to model cutting, tearing and grinding without food handling.
phases.pupils: Match each tooth group to its shape and job, then explain one match to a partner.

phases.teacher: Use three unlabelled images and check the match between name and function for each pupil.
phases.pupils: Label all three types and match cutting, tearing and grinding to them.

phases.teacher: Ask which tooth is useful for grinding and why its shape helps.
phases.pupils: Point to a molar and name its broad surface.

plans.follow_up: Revisit teeth whose shape pupils identified but whose job they confused.

plans.label: Lesson 11
plans.title: Structure of a tooth
plans.objective: Label enamel, dentine, gum, blood vessels and nerves on a simple tooth diagram.
plans.materials: Large tooth cross-section, word bank and individual outline cards.

phases.teacher: Show the outside of a tooth and ask what the cutaway view could reveal.
phases.pupils: Suggest one part that cannot be seen from outside.

phases.teacher: Trace the enamel, dentine, gum, blood vessels and nerves on a diagram with five colour-coded prompts.
phases.pupils: Place five word cards at the correct sites and compare enamel and dentine positions.

phases.teacher: Give an unlabelled outline with five arrows. Check each pupil’s labels against the diagram.
phases.pupils: Label enamel, dentine, gum, blood vessels and nerves on the outline.

phases.teacher: Ask pupils to point to the outer hard layer and the parts inside the tooth.
phases.pupils: Name enamel and distinguish it from the inside structures.

plans.follow_up: Recheck the locations of enamel and dentine using a layered diagram.

plans.label: Lesson 12
plans.title: Milk and permanent teeth
plans.objective: Compare two features of milk and permanent teeth in a two-column table.
plans.materials: Milk and permanent tooth-set diagrams, comparison table and counting counters.

phases.teacher: Show two tooth charts with covered headings and ask what can be counted or compared.
phases.pupils: Identify one difference visible between charts.

phases.teacher: Give pairs labelled textbook diagrams to compare quantity, replacement and features visible in the drawings. Model evidence for one cell.
phases.pupils: Count and compare the charts, then enter paired observations in a two-column table.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to produce two fair comparisons. Check each comparison refers to both tooth sets.
phases.pupils: Submit two comparisons with the same feature shown across the two columns.

phases.teacher: Ask what replaces milk teeth as children grow.
phases.pupils: Identify permanent teeth and state one other difference from the table.

plans.follow_up: Recheck paired comparisons using the same feature on both sides.

plans.label: Lesson 13
plans.title: Care for teeth and explain why
plans.objective: Use a labelled diagram to explain how one dental care practice protects the tooth.
plans.materials: Tooth model, large demonstration brush, care routine cards and tooth outlines.

phases.teacher: Show two dental care routines and ask which protects a tooth and how.
phases.pupils: Choose a routine and suggest one reason.

phases.teacher: Use a model to demonstrate where a brush reaches and how a care routine applies to the tooth surface. Offer ordinary scenarios to discuss.
phases.pupils: Practise on the model, then mark which part of a tooth the chosen care action protects.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil’s diagram and explanation for a correct part, practice and reason.
phases.pupils: Label the tooth area, show one care practice and explain how it helps protect the tooth.

phases.teacher: Ask pupils to name one routine they can explain to someone else.
phases.pupils: Give a care action and link it to the tooth or gum area shown.

plans.follow_up: Help pupils connect the care action to the part protected.

plans.label: Lesson 14
plans.title: Classify foods
plans.objective: Sort familiar foods into food classes and give another example for each assigned class.
plans.materials: Familiar food picture cards, food-class headings and example slips.

phases.teacher: Show pictures of rice and fish and ask how they could be placed into different food classes.
phases.pupils: Name a likely class for each card.

phases.teacher: Model sorting single foods by the food class shown in the textbook. Give each group a small selection and the available class headings.
phases.pupils: Sort each card under a heading and propose one further example for each assigned class.

phases.teacher: Allocate two or three class headings per pupil, then check correct placement and one new example for each.
phases.pupils: Sort the cards and write another example beside every heading assigned.

phases.teacher: Ask for one way to justify a class choice when two foods look similar.
phases.pupils: Name the food class and point to a named example that supports it.

plans.follow_up: Recheck whole mixed dishes separately from single-food examples.

plans.label: Lesson 15
plans.title: Explain why food classes matter
plans.objective: Match three food classes to their roles in the body and justify one choice.
plans.materials: Food-class cards, function cards and short scenario slips.

phases.teacher: Ask what food helps with when someone needs energy to move.
phases.pupils: Propose a food class and give a reason.

phases.teacher: Model “class–role” with one example. Give groups short needs such as energy, growth or healthy digestion and cards to match.
phases.pupils: Match food classes to their roles, then explain a match using one relevant body need.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to match three classes to three roles and justify one selection.
phases.pupils: Submit three class–role pairs and give a reason for one pair.

phases.teacher: Compare two distinct roles and ask for an example of each.
phases.pupils: Name the classes and explain one difference in their roles.

plans.follow_up: Use body-role prompts to clarify mixed-up class–role pairs.

plans.label: Lesson 16
plans.title: Plan a balanced meal
plans.objective: Propose one meal and explain how its components fit the food pyramid.
plans.materials: Food pyramid diagram, meal cards and plate templates.

phases.teacher: Show a one-food meal picture and ask which parts of a balanced meal are missing.
phases.pupils: Name one missing food group and propose a food example.

phases.teacher: Model using the food pyramid to check variety and relative proportions. Ask pairs to improve a simple meal while keeping it realistic.
phases.pupils: Build a meal with cards, identify where each component fits in the pyramid and explain one revision.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil a blank plate. Check the proposed meal and its explanation against the pyramid.
phases.pupils: Draw or list a meal and explain why the selected components fit the food pyramid.

phases.teacher: Invite pupils to give one change that improves a sample meal.
phases.pupils: Name the food added or adjusted and connect it to its place in the pyramid.

plans.follow_up: Recheck pupils’ use of variety and the suggested proportions.

plans.label: Lesson 17
plans.title: Explain an imbalanced diet
plans.objective: Compare two menus and explain one likely effect and one improvement for the less balanced menu.
plans.materials: Two illustrated menus, food pyramid and comparison slips.

phases.teacher: Show two sample menus and ask which contains a wider variety of suitable foods.
phases.pupils: Choose a menu and point to visible evidence.

phases.teacher: Guide groups to compare variety and proportion, then model linking one repeated imbalance to a likely effect without judging individuals.
phases.pupils: Mark strengths and gaps in each menu, then discuss realistic changes the less balanced menu could make.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil identifies an evidence-based difference, one possible effect and one specific improvement.
phases.pupils: Compare the two menus and state one likely effect and one change for the less balanced menu.

phases.teacher: Ask pupils why a single sample menu is different from a long-term diet.
phases.pupils: Explain that repeated patterns affect the body over time.

plans.follow_up: Check changes address an identified imbalance in the menu.

plans.label: Lesson 18
plans.title: Describe digestion
plans.objective: Explain in simple terms how food is broken down so the body can use nutrients.
plans.materials: Food-piece illustrations, digestion sequence cards and a body diagram.

phases.teacher: Ask whether the body can use a large piece of food in the same form it is swallowed.
phases.pupils: Suggest what happens to food after chewing and swallowing.

phases.teacher: Use picture cards to model food breaking down into smaller components and show where digestion occurs. Build a simple class sequence without using real food.
phases.pupils: Place cards in an evidence-based order and say how the body can make use of nutrients after breaking food down.

phases.teacher: Invite each pupil to give a short oral or written explanation with both breakdown and purpose.
phases.pupils: Explain in simple terms what digestion changes and why that helps the body use nutrients.

phases.teacher: Ask a pupil to complete “Digestion breaks food down so …”.
phases.pupils: Finish the sentence using a body-use or nutrients statement.

plans.follow_up: Check explanations link breakdown to the body’s use of nutrients.

plans.label: Lesson 19
plans.title: Trace the path of food
plans.objective: Place mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine in the correct order and identify the exit.
plans.materials: Digestive-pathway diagram, movable organ labels and arrows.

phases.teacher: Show an outline of the human body and ask where food enters.
phases.pupils: Point to the mouth and name a likely next place.

phases.teacher: Model following one continuous route using arrow cards. Give groups scrambled cards for the organs and the exit.
phases.pupils: Arrange mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. Add the exit and trace the full route.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil the unlabelled path and six movable labels, including the exit. Check order independently.
phases.pupils: Order the five organs correctly and identify the anus as the exit for undigested waste.

phases.teacher: Ask which organ follows the stomach along the route.
phases.pupils: Point to and name the small intestine.

plans.follow_up: Rehearse the sequence where pupils mixed up the two intestines.

plans.label: Lesson 20
plans.title: Explain what happens after digestion
plans.objective: Use arrows in a diagram to distinguish nutrient absorption from the removal of undigested waste.
plans.materials: Digestive diagram with coloured arrows, nutrient/waste cards and individual diagrams.

phases.teacher: Show two arrows after the small intestine and ask what could travel by different routes.
phases.pupils: Suggest what happens to useful nutrients and undigested material.

phases.teacher: Model arrows from the small intestine to the blood and along the digestive tract toward the exit. Use cards to contrast what each route carries.
phases.pupils: Place nutrient and waste cards on the diagram, trace the arrows and explain the two processes to a partner.

phases.teacher: Check individual diagrams use two correctly labelled routes with a phrase for each process.
phases.pupils: Draw and label nutrient absorption and the removal of undigested waste using different arrows.

phases.teacher: Ask which arrow carries nutrients to the body.
phases.pupils: Point to the route toward the blood and explain why the routes differ.

plans.follow_up: Correct confusion about absorption and the route out of the body.

plans.label: Review 01
plans.title: Humans
plans.objective: Explain the links between teeth, balanced meals and digestion using a diagram.
plans.materials: Tooth images, meal cards, digestion route and concept-map sheet.

phases.teacher: Show a tooth, a meal and a stomach picture. Ask for a connection between any two.
phases.pupils: Explain one link using a fact from the unit.

phases.teacher: Model one connecting arrow with a verb. Ask pairs to place all three images and discuss how to connect them.
phases.pupils: Make a draft map linking teeth, balanced food and digestion using words along the arrows.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil’s diagram has all three ideas and accurate labelled links.
phases.pupils: Make a map explaining how teeth start breaking food down, how a balanced meal supplies nutrients and how digestion lets the body use them.

phases.teacher: Ask which link explains why chewing helps.
phases.pupils: Point to the relevant arrow and explain it in one sentence.

plans.follow_up: Revisit only the link still missing from the concept map.

plans.label: Lesson 21
plans.title: Group animals by what they eat
plans.objective: Classify six examples as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores using food evidence.
plans.materials: Six animal pictures with diet records, group labels and classification grids.

phases.teacher: Show a rabbit food card and a tiger food card and compare what the two animals eat.
phases.pupils: Describe the food evidence for each card.

phases.teacher: Model how plant, animal or both kinds of food support the three diet groups. Give groups six illustrated cases with diet evidence.
phases.pupils: Sort each case using the diet shown and record at least one piece of evidence for the classification.

phases.teacher: Give an independent grid. Check six classifications and the evidence used instead of the animal’s appearance.
phases.pupils: Classify the six animals as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores using the diet records.

phases.teacher: Ask how the evidence changes when a card lists plants and animals.
phases.pupils: Name omnivore and cite both types of food.

plans.follow_up: Correct group choices based only on size, teeth or appearance.

plans.label: Lesson 22
plans.title: Infer the group from an animal's diet
plans.objective: Use a food record to infer the group of an unfamiliar animal and justify the answer.
plans.materials: Four-day feeding log cards, diet group chart and evidence slips.

phases.teacher: Show a single feeding observation and ask what additional detail might help identify a diet group.
phases.pupils: Say what food is recorded and propose what else to observe.

phases.teacher: Model reading a record across several days rather than relying on the animal’s shape. Give pairs an unfamiliar animal’s food log.
phases.pupils: Highlight plant and animal foods and infer the likely group from the full log.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil a second short record. Check that the conclusion names the correct group and cites recorded foods.
phases.pupils: State the likely group and quote or paraphrase one or two food observations that justify it.

phases.teacher: Ask whether a record of one meal is always enough to classify a diet.
phases.pupils: Explain why more observations may change the inference.

plans.follow_up: Check evidence is taken from the record rather than an assumed diet.

plans.label: Lesson 23
plans.title: Compare animal teeth
plans.objective: Compare two dental features across three animal groups and relate one feature to diet.
plans.materials: Clear tooth photos or diagrams of three animals, comparison grids and pencils.

phases.teacher: Compare two close-up tooth images and ask what looks alike or different.
phases.pupils: Name a visible tooth feature without naming the diet yet.

phases.teacher: Set out herbivore, carnivore and omnivore diagrams with diet labels. Model comparing a broad grinding surface and a pointed tearing surface.
phases.pupils: Compare two features for each pictured group and connect one observed feature to the type of food eaten.

phases.teacher: Ask for an individual entry showing two comparisons across all three groups and one evidence-based link.
phases.pupils: Complete the grid and relate one specific tooth feature to the animal’s diet.

phases.teacher: Ask what information would confirm a prediction about diet made from teeth alone.
phases.pupils: Propose checking what the animal is observed eating.

plans.follow_up: Revisit evidence from tooth shape and feeding behaviour.

plans.label: Lesson 24
plans.title: Explain evidence about animal diets
plans.objective: Present a classification with one supporting observation and explain an example of changed feeding behaviour.
plans.materials: Food record cards, a teacher-made before–after feeding scenario and presentation sheets.

phases.teacher: Show an animal feeding record with one change between two days.
phases.pupils: Describe what changed in the record before suggesting why.

phases.teacher: Guide groups to separate the usual diet classification from a reported behaviour change. Model how to cite a recorded food item.
phases.pupils: Prepare a brief report naming the group, a supporting observation and one possible reason for the observed change.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil gives evidence for the group and explanation for the scenario rather than a claim about all animals in the group.
phases.pupils: Present a diet classification, name one supporting food observation and explain the behaviour change in the case.

phases.teacher: Ask which part of the report is evidence and which part is explanation.
phases.pupils: Identify one direct observation and one interpretation.

plans.follow_up: Recheck that the explanation stays within the evidence provided.

plans.label: Lesson 25
plans.title: Identify ways plants reproduce
plans.objective: Match at least four familiar plants to a method of reproduction using specimen cards.
plans.materials: Specimen photos or cards of seeds, stem cuttings, leaf plantlets and other verified examples.

phases.teacher: Show one seed and a photograph of a plantlet on a leaf.
phases.pupils: Describe where each new plant might start.

phases.teacher: Model matching a plant to a method using an observed clue. Give groups at least four vetted specimens or clear photos with method cards.
phases.pupils: Identify the visible clue and match each plant to its method of reproduction.

phases.teacher: Shuffle the same examples and check each pupil can independently match at least four.
phases.pupils: Match four familiar plants to their reproduction methods using the cards.

phases.teacher: Ask one pupil to explain why a particular example was not matched to seeds.
phases.pupils: Point to the observable plant part and name its method.

plans.follow_up: Recheck examples where the growing part was overlooked.

plans.label: Lesson 26
plans.title: Explain why reproduction matters
plans.objective: Draw a cause-and-effect diagram linking new plants to food, habitats or the survival of a species.
plans.materials: Plant photos, picture cards for food and habitats and arrow-label slips.

phases.teacher: Ask what might happen in a place where old plants die and no new plants grow.
phases.pupils: Suggest one effect for an animal or a person.

phases.teacher: Model a two-step cause-and-effect chain using one familiar plant. Give groups context cards for food, shelter or species survival.
phases.pupils: Arrange arrows to show how new plants replace old plants and what that allows organisms to continue using.

phases.teacher: Check each individual diagram links new plants to at least one supported outcome.
phases.pupils: Draw and label a cause-and-effect sequence for food, habitat or survival of a species.

phases.teacher: Ask what would change if the first part of the chain stopped.
phases.pupils: Use the diagram to name one consequence of reduced reproduction.

plans.follow_up: Check the arrows explain a consequence rather than list unrelated facts.

plans.label: Lesson 27
plans.title: Investigate more than one propagation method
plans.objective: Set up two teacher-approved methods for one suitable plant and start a dated observation log.
plans.materials: Teacher-prepared sweet potato material for two growth methods, labelled containers and observation logs.

phases.teacher: Show a teacher-held stem cutting and a sprouting tuber from the same kind of plant.
phases.pupils: Identify the part being used in each method.

phases.teacher: Prepare compatible containers, label each method and demonstrate starting both using teacher-approved material. Guide pupils to document initial conditions and agree a safe observation routine.
phases.pupils: Set up or assist at two supervised stations, label both methods and record the date and starting observations for each.

phases.teacher: Check each pair has both labelled setups, a dated baseline and a named feature to follow. Ask each pupil to explain a label.
phases.pupils: Make the initial entries for both methods and state one visible change to look for in follow-up observations.

phases.teacher: Ask how the class will distinguish the two setups at the next observation.
phases.pupils: Refer to the method and date labels and agree when to check them.

plans.follow_up: Check both methods are logged from the start and follow-up is arranged.

plans.label: Lesson 28
plans.title: Report the plant project
plans.objective: Compare dated records from both propagation methods and support one conclusion using class records or mature samples.
plans.materials: Dated records from Lesson 27, prepared comparison records or mature samples and a chart template.

phases.teacher: Show two dated entries and ask what can be compared at the same point in the records.
phases.pupils: Name one feature such as first visible new roots or shoots.

phases.teacher: Model aligning observations by date. If growth is incomplete, give clearly labelled teacher records or mature samples alongside the class log.
phases.pupils: Compare both methods, cite dated details and explain what can or cannot yet be concluded.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil’s conclusion cites an observation from both methods or names the prepared comparison source.
phases.pupils: Summarise two dated observations and support one conclusion using the records or mature samples.

phases.teacher: Ask why observations taken on different days should be labelled.
phases.pupils: Explain how dates make a comparison fairer to interpret.

plans.follow_up: Revisit conclusions that assume unobserved growth.

plans.label: Review 02
plans.title: Animals and Plants
plans.objective: Sort four examples by diet or reproduction method and explain two selections.
plans.materials: Two animal diet cards, two plant propagation cards, labels and an evidence sheet.

phases.teacher: Show a diet entry and a cutting photograph and ask what each can establish.
phases.pupils: Identify which detail helps group an animal or identify a plant method.

phases.teacher: Give pairs four review cases and model an evidence sentence on a separate example.
phases.pupils: Sort both animal and plant cases and prepare reasons using the recorded food or plant part.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil groups all four cases and explains two choices using evidence.
phases.pupils: Submit four classifications and write two reasons drawn from the cards.

phases.teacher: Ask why being able to point to a clue helps a reader check the answer.
phases.pupils: Name one clue from an animal or plant case.

plans.follow_up: Review any category pupils chose without referring to evidence.

plans.label: Lesson 29
plans.title: Recognise area and volume units
plans.objective: Select cm², cm³, mL or L for four examples and explain the choice for one example.
plans.materials: Unit cards, squares, cubes, a measuring cylinder, a litre jug and four use-case images.

phases.teacher: Compare a square tile, a cube and a water container.
phases.pupils: Say which example shows a surface or holds a volume.

phases.teacher: Match cm² to the square unit, cm³ to the cube and mL/L to liquid measures. Show the difference in practical scale between a small cylinder and a jug.
phases.pupils: Choose the suitable unit for each use-case image and discuss near choices in pairs.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil chooses four appropriate units and justifies one choice by attribute or scale.
phases.pupils: Select cm², cm³, mL or L for the four items and explain one selection.

phases.teacher: Ask which unit measures a surface and which unit could be used for a small liquid quantity.
phases.pupils: Name cm² and mL and describe the difference.

plans.follow_up: Check cm² and cm³ are linked to area and volume respectively.

plans.label: Lesson 30
plans.title: Measure a regular area
plans.objective: Cover a regular outline with 1 cm squares and give the total in cm².
plans.materials: One-centimetre square tiles, regular outlines, a 1 cm grid and recording slips.

phases.teacher: Show a rectangle on centimetre paper and ask what part is measured by area.
phases.pupils: Point to the inside surface rather than the outline.

phases.teacher: Model fitting tiles edge-to-edge without gaps and counting each tile once. Give pairs different regular outlines.
phases.pupils: Cover a rectangle or square with 1 cm squares and compare counts by rows or columns.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to cover a fresh outline and record its area. Check coverage and unit.
phases.pupils: Make the tile count and record the total in cm².

phases.teacher: Ask why a gap or overlap changes the result.
phases.pupils: Describe whether coverage would be too little or counted twice.

plans.follow_up: Recheck systematic counting and square centimetre units.

plans.label: Lesson 31
plans.title: Estimate an irregular area
plans.objective: Estimate the area of a leaf outline on a centimetre grid and explain how partial squares were counted.
plans.materials: Leaf outlines, transparent centimetre grids, pencils and tally sheets.

phases.teacher: Show a leaf outline over a grid and ask why some squares are only partly covered.
phases.pupils: Identify one full square and one partial square.

phases.teacher: Demonstrate counting full squares and using a consistent approximation for parts, such as pairing halves. Ask pairs to agree and document their rule.
phases.pupils: Mark full squares, estimate partial squares and use both counts to estimate the leaf’s area.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil gives an area in cm² and explains how partial squares contributed.
phases.pupils: Estimate a new leaf outline and show the full-square count and chosen partial-square rule.

phases.teacher: Ask why two valid estimates of the same outline can differ slightly.
phases.pupils: Connect the difference to choices about partly covered squares.

plans.follow_up: Recheck estimates that omit partial areas or count them all as full.

plans.label: Lesson 32
plans.title: Measure the volume of a box
plans.objective: Fill a small rectangular container with 1 cm cubes and record its volume in cm³.
plans.materials: Small box with whole-centimetre dimensions, 1 cm cubes and layer diagrams.

phases.teacher: Show an empty box and ask how cubes can measure the space inside.
phases.pupils: Propose filling the box with equal-sized cubes.

phases.teacher: Model making a full first layer with no space and recording its cube count. Guide pairs to fill the remaining layers.
phases.pupils: Pack cubes without gaps, count cubes in each layer and record the total.

phases.teacher: Check the pupil’s box model or labelled layers. Confirm a correct total in cm³.
phases.pupils: Fill a small box independently or show the checked layer counts and write its volume in cm³.

phases.teacher: Ask which three dimensions a cube measures.
phases.pupils: Explain that the measured space has length, width and height.

plans.follow_up: Recheck pupils count all layers rather than just the bottom layer.

plans.label: Lesson 33
plans.title: Measure a liquid volume
plans.objective: Choose a suitable measuring cylinder and record two readings at eye level in mL.
plans.materials: Small measuring cylinders, coloured water, pouring trays and a reading table.

phases.teacher: Show two drawings of the same cylinder viewed above and at eye level.
phases.pupils: Identify which viewing position gives a reliable reading.

phases.teacher: Model choosing a cylinder that holds the sample and has usable scale divisions. Place the cylinder on a level surface and show the bottom of the water meniscus at eye level.
phases.pupils: Choose a cylinder, pour with supervision and take two eye-level readings while a partner records the units.

phases.teacher: Observe each pupil reading one sample and check that both readings are recorded correctly in mL.
phases.pupils: Read a cylinder at eye level and submit both mL values using the scale shown.

phases.teacher: Ask how to read a line between numbered marks.
phases.pupils: State the value of a scale division and use it to explain a reading.

plans.follow_up: Correct oversize cylinder selection and reading above or below eye level.

plans.label: Lesson 34
plans.title: Calculate displaced volume
plans.objective: Record the initial and final water levels for a submerged object and calculate the difference.
plans.materials: Plastic measuring cylinders, water, nonfloating objects that fit, thread and trays.

phases.teacher: Show a water level before and after an object is submerged and ask what changed.
phases.pupils: State that the water level rose and suggest how to quantify the change.

phases.teacher: Model choosing a suitable object, reading the initial level and lowering it fully without overflow or air bubbles. Record both levels before subtracting.
phases.pupils: Repeat the paired readings with a teacher-approved object, list them in order and calculate the difference.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil records initial and final mL values, subtracts in the correct order and identifies displaced volume.
phases.pupils: Measure or interpret the two readings and calculate the displaced volume with a unit.

phases.teacher: Ask whether the final water level alone gives the object’s volume.
phases.pupils: Use the readings to explain why the change is needed.

plans.follow_up: Recheck readings and the order of subtraction.

plans.label: Lesson 35
plans.title: Explain an area or volume method
plans.objective: Present two measurements with units and justify one tool or technique used.
plans.materials: A grid, a cylinder, outline cards, measured samples and evidence cards.

phases.teacher: Present two claims with missing units and ask why they cannot be checked properly.
phases.pupils: Identify the missing units or information about the tools.

phases.teacher: Set up an area method station and a volume method station. Model describing one technique and explaining why the selected tool fits the job.
phases.pupils: Make or check two measurements, record units and prepare reasons for a method choice.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to show two results and justify one tool or method from the evidence.
phases.pupils: Present both measured values with units and explain one tool or technique used.

phases.teacher: Ask what a different class would need to repeat the method.
phases.pupils: Name one detail about the tool, unit or technique that needs to be recorded.

plans.follow_up: Revisit justifications that name only the tool without a reason.

plans.label: Lesson 36
plans.title: Investigate floating and sinking
plans.objective: Record the behaviour of four items in water and propose one explanation based on the observations.
plans.materials: Clear water tubs, trays, cork, plastic cap, metal washer and stone.

phases.teacher: Show four small objects and ask where each will go in water.
phases.pupils: Predict one float or sink result and say what could be observed.

phases.teacher: Ask groups to lower each object gently in the same water, one at a time. Model recording a surface or bottom observation without pushing the object.
phases.pupils: Test all four items, record their behaviour and compare results to predictions.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil records four results and supplies one explanation based on a contrast or observation.
phases.pupils: Submit the table and describe a supported explanation of one result or contrast.

phases.teacher: Ask why size alone is insufficient as an explanation.
phases.pupils: Cite two items whose results do not fit a size-only rule.

plans.follow_up: Review predictions that used only weight or size without evidence.

plans.label: Lesson 37
plans.title: Compare density with water
plans.objective: Use fresh-water observations to infer which tested items are denser or less dense than water.
plans.materials: Fresh-water results from Lesson 36, stable tubs and density statement cards.

phases.teacher: Show two test results that behaved differently in fresh water.
phases.pupils: Identify which example stayed at the surface and which went to the bottom.

phases.teacher: Explain how these tested items can be compared with water using the float/sink records. Keep the claim tied to the objects in the investigation.
phases.pupils: Place tested items under denser or less dense than fresh water and attach the observation used for each choice.

phases.teacher: Check individual classifications and ask for one short inference from the table.
phases.pupils: Write the density comparison for each tested item and point to its supporting freshwater behaviour.

phases.teacher: Ask what the comparison uses as its reference.
phases.pupils: Identify fresh water and state how it was used to compare the items.

plans.follow_up: Recheck pupils do not rank the exact densities of the different items from float/sink data.

plans.label: Lesson 38
plans.title: Make water denser
plans.objective: Compare an object's behaviour in fresh and salt water and explain the change using density.
plans.materials: Two transparent cups, fresh water, teacher-prepared salt solution, small potato pieces and trays.

phases.teacher: Show two similar cups and ask what can be changed while using the same type of test object.
phases.pupils: Suggest comparing plain water with dissolved salt while keeping the object consistent.

phases.teacher: Guide a pre-tested demonstration with water and salt solution. Ask the class to observe the same object placed gently in both liquids.
phases.pupils: Record its behaviour in fresh and salt water and compare the two outcomes using the class observations.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil records both outcomes and explains that dissolving salt increased the water’s density.
phases.pupils: Submit a comparison and connect a change in floating or sinking to the denser solution.

phases.teacher: Ask why comparing two different objects would weaken the result.
phases.pupils: Explain that the same test object helps isolate the difference between the liquids.

plans.follow_up: Recheck the density comparison of the liquids and what the results show.

plans.label: Lesson 39
plans.title: Explain a use of density
plans.objective: Create a labelled drawing and use an observation from class to explain a real-life example.
plans.materials: Floating marker and flotation-device images, class results and drawing sheets.

phases.teacher: Show a floating marker and ask which classroom test it resembles.
phases.pupils: Name an object observed floating and describe what it did.

phases.teacher: Ask groups to choose a familiar application. Model using an arrow or label to link the observation to why the object stays at the surface.
phases.pupils: Prepare a labelled sketch and explain the real-life use using one classroom observation.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil labels the object and water and explicitly links an actual observation to the application.
phases.pupils: Submit a sketch and write an explanation that names the classroom result used.

phases.teacher: Ask what might change if the material or shape were changed.
phases.pupils: Suggest one change and say how it could be tested safely.

plans.follow_up: Strengthen links between the example and the specific observation.

plans.label: Lesson 40
plans.title: Test substances using litmus
plans.objective: Record changes to red and blue litmus for three teacher-prepared samples and classify each sample.
plans.materials: Red and blue litmus, droppers, trays, water and teacher-prepared dilute sample cups.

phases.teacher: Display the two litmus colours and read the safety rule for unknown liquids.
phases.pupils: State how the droppers and indicators will be used without tasting or touching samples.

phases.teacher: Demonstrate one drop on each colour of litmus. Give three teacher-prepared samples with separate droppers and provide a colour key.
phases.pupils: Observe changes for both indicators, record initial and final colours and classify each sample with the key.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil records both indicators for all three samples and gives a classification supported by the observed pattern.
phases.pupils: Submit the three-row table and explain what the paired colours show for one sample.

phases.teacher: Ask why one unchanged strip alone is insufficient for a neutral claim.
phases.pupils: Explain that both red and blue strips need to be considered.

plans.follow_up: Recheck paired readings and the definition of neutral.

plans.label: Lesson 41
plans.title: Compare reported properties safely
plans.objective: Use teacher-provided descriptions to compare examples and explain why taste or touch cannot identify an unknown substance.
plans.materials: Teacher-supplied descriptions of familiar examples, property comparison table and safety cards.

phases.teacher: Show a labelled picture and a container marked unknown. Ask which sources can provide safe evidence.
phases.pupils: Choose reliable written descriptions or an appropriate indicator with teacher supervision.

phases.teacher: Provide descriptions of known materials. Guide pupils to distinguish a reported property from a tested result and model the safety response to an unknown sample.
phases.pupils: Compare two described examples on a chart and propose a safe method when a substance is unknown.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil compares examples using the descriptions and explains why tasting or touching unknowns is unsafe and inconclusive.
phases.pupils: Submit two comparisons and a safety reason with a safer source of evidence.

phases.teacher: Ask how to respond if a classmate suggests touching an unknown liquid.
phases.pupils: Explain the class safety rule and identify a safer evidence source.

plans.follow_up: Recheck descriptions are cited as reported properties, without asking pupils to test sensations.

plans.label: Lesson 42
plans.title: Compare other indicators
plans.objective: Compare the colour changes of a teacher-prepared plant indicator and litmus for the same samples.
plans.materials: Teacher-made red cabbage indicator, litmus, droppers, safe teacher-prepared samples and a comparison grid.

phases.teacher: Show the plant indicator and litmus separately and ask how to compare their responses fairly.
phases.pupils: Suggest using the same samples and separate clean droppers.

phases.teacher: Demonstrate the procedures and guide pupils to compare results using a teacher-provided colour reference for the plant indicator.
phases.pupils: Record both indicators for the same labelled samples. Note a similarity and a difference between the ways results are shown.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil has paired observations for the same samples and gives one accurate comparison.
phases.pupils: Complete the grid and describe one observed similarity or difference supported by the colour records.

phases.teacher: Ask why the class needs the supplied plant-indicator colour reference.
phases.pupils: Explain that different indicators can show different colours for the same type of substance.

plans.follow_up: Correct classifications that assume plant indicator and litmus use identical colours.

plans.label: Lesson 43
plans.title: Report indicator results
plans.objective: Summarise results in a three-row table and draw a conclusion based on colour changes.
plans.materials: Class indicator records, sample labels and a three-row table template.

phases.teacher: Show a record missing its conclusion and ask which columns provide evidence.
phases.pupils: Point to the result columns and name one useful value.

phases.teacher: Model a three-row table with sample, indicator observation and classification. Ask groups to verify their entries against the indicator key.
phases.pupils: Summarise their observations and discuss which colour changes justify one chosen claim.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil’s three-row table and require a conclusion grounded in a recorded result.
phases.pupils: Submit the table and explain one sample classification using its recorded colour changes.

phases.teacher: Present an unlabelled result and ask what detail would make it interpretable.
phases.pupils: Specify the indicator colour before or after the test and the sample identity.

plans.follow_up: Review conclusions that omit the observed colour change.

plans.label: Review 03
plans.title: Measurement, Density and Indicators
plans.objective: Correct one measurement and explain a result from a density or litmus table.
plans.materials: A misread scale card, a measured-area record and two short density or litmus tables.

phases.teacher: Show a measurement read from the wrong scale mark.
phases.pupils: Identify what looks wrong and propose a check.

phases.teacher: Review units and one method from Unit 6. Offer a choice of a density and a litmus evidence table from the taught units.
phases.pupils: Correct a sample measurement and circle the table evidence explaining a separate result.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil has one corrected measurement and one valid interpretation linked to a table entry.
phases.pupils: Submit the corrected reading with units and one evidence-based explanation from a density or litmus table.

phases.teacher: Ask which details allow someone else to check the pupil’s reasoning.
phases.pupils: Name a unit, a scale mark or a relevant table entry.

plans.follow_up: Recheck the specific method or interpretation that produced the error.

plans.label: Lesson 44
plans.title: Identify Solar System members
plans.objective: Label the Sun and the eight planets in order and name two other types of Solar System objects.
plans.materials: Sun and planet cards, orbit strip and object cards for asteroids and comets.

phases.teacher: Show the Sun and Earth cards and ask where the Sun belongs in the model.
phases.pupils: Place the Sun centrally and identify Earth as a planet.

phases.teacher: Use the textbook sequence to check the eight planet cards. Demonstrate adding two other objects to an illustrated Solar System without treating them as planets.
phases.pupils: Build the Sun and planet sequence, then sort asteroid and comet cards as separate object types.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil labels the Sun and eight planets in order and names two other object types.
phases.pupils: Label a sequence from the Sun outwards and add asteroids and comets to the list of other objects.

phases.teacher: Ask pupils to name Earth’s neighbouring planets in the order from the Sun.
phases.pupils: Identify Venus and Mars from the completed order.

plans.follow_up: Practise the part of the planet sequence the pupil still reverses.

plans.label: Lesson 45
plans.title: Compare planet temperatures
plans.objective: Use a supplied data chart to state the general trend with distance and explain why Venus is an exception.
plans.materials: Teacher-supplied chart of relative distances and representative temperatures, axes and comparison slips.

phases.teacher: Ask which of Mercury and Venus is closer to the Sun before revealing the data.
phases.pupils: Identify Mercury from the planet sequence and predict which might be hotter.

phases.teacher: Read both columns of the chart. Guide groups to describe the broad trend and compare Mercury and Venus using the chart and the textbook explanation of Venus’s atmosphere.
phases.pupils: Order examples by distance, compare their temperatures and mark Venus as an exception to the simple distance prediction.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil states the general trend, cites Mercury/Venus evidence and links Venus’s high temperature to heat trapped by its atmosphere.
phases.pupils: Submit a trend statement and one evidence-backed explanation of Venus as an exception.

phases.teacher: Ask why distance is useful but insufficient in this example.
phases.pupils: Explain that atmosphere can affect a planet’s temperature.

plans.follow_up: Check pupils distinguish the general trend from the Venus comparison.

plans.label: Lesson 46
plans.title: Model orbits around the Sun
plans.objective: Demonstrate an orbit and distinguish a planet's revolution from its rotation.
plans.materials: Tabletop Sun and planet models, a marked side of the planet ball and orbit arrows.

phases.teacher: Spin the ball in place and ask whether it has travelled round the Sun.
phases.pupils: Identify a spin without an orbit.

phases.teacher: Show rotation about the model’s axis and revolution around the Sun separately, then together. Set out an arrow track for partners to use.
phases.pupils: Take turns modelling one complete orbit and one spin. Use the marked side to show the difference.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to identify and demonstrate both motions. Check the model travels around the Sun for revolution.
phases.pupils: Demonstrate the orbit and distinguish revolution from rotation in an explanation.

phases.teacher: Ask which motion determines a planet’s year in the model.
phases.pupils: Point to the orbit and name revolution.

plans.follow_up: Recheck that rotation is about the planet’s own axis.

plans.label: Lesson 47
plans.title: Compare revolution times
plans.objective: Order four planets by their period of revolution and relate the pattern to distance from the Sun.
plans.materials: Four printed planet data cards, number strip and distance labels.

phases.teacher: Show two cards with different revolution periods and ask how they can be compared.
phases.pupils: Identify the relevant values and check their units.

phases.teacher: Give four planets with periods in consistent units from a checked teaching chart. Model ordering one pair by period, then comparing distances.
phases.pupils: Arrange planets from the shortest to longest period and use a separate distance row to look for a pattern.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil orders all four and gives a distance–period relationship supported by the cards.
phases.pupils: Produce the ordered list and state how the period generally changes with distance from the Sun.

phases.teacher: Ask what one revolution period measures.
phases.pupils: Explain it is the time for one trip around the Sun.

plans.follow_up: Review units and correct any comparison using a rotation period.

plans.label: Lesson 48
plans.title: Communicate Solar System findings
plans.objective: Use a diagram and a data point to explain one relationship in the Solar System.
plans.materials: Planet diagrams, checked temperature or period chart, blank poster sheets and evidence prompts.

phases.teacher: Show a planet claim without supporting evidence and ask what could strengthen it.
phases.pupils: Suggest one matching data point or a labelled part of a model.

phases.teacher: Model combining a diagram with a number or recorded comparison. Invite pairs to present one relationship about planet temperature, distance or revolution.
phases.pupils: Prepare a labelled diagram and select a data point that directly supports the explanation.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil names the relationship, labels the diagram accurately and points to a matching data point.
phases.pupils: Explain the relationship in one minute or on a written card using both the diagram and the data point.

phases.teacher: Ask the class to identify the evidence in one presentation.
phases.pupils: Name the relevant label or data point and say how it supports the idea.

plans.follow_up: Recheck data points chosen only for interest rather than evidence.

plans.label: Lesson 49
plans.title: Identify a pulley and its purpose
plans.objective: Label the wheel and rope of a pulley and describe what the device helps people do.
plans.materials: Fixed pulley demonstration, light attached load and outline cards.

phases.teacher: Show a photo of a flag raising system and ask what guides the line.
phases.pupils: Identify the wheel or rope in the picture.

phases.teacher: Point out the wheel and rope on a secure tabletop demonstration. Slowly raise the light load and trace the moving line.
phases.pupils: Observe the demonstration, trace the rope over the wheel and tell a partner what the pulley helps people move.

phases.teacher: Give each pupil an outline to label. Check wheel, rope and a correct purpose statement.
phases.pupils: Label the wheel and rope and explain one way the pulley helps move a load.

phases.teacher: Ask how the line moves when the load goes up.
phases.pupils: Use the demonstration to describe one direction of motion.

plans.follow_up: Recheck the parts that guide the rope and hold the load.

plans.label: Lesson 50
plans.title: Explain a fixed pulley
plans.objective: Use arrows to show the direction of pull and the direction of load movement on a model.
plans.materials: Secure fixed pulley stands, soft cords, very light test loads and arrow cards.

phases.teacher: Hold a pulley diagram and ask which way to pull to make the load rise.
phases.pupils: Predict the pull and movement directions with two arrows.

phases.teacher: Demonstrate changing the direction of pull using a secure model. Give pairs a checked station with a light test load.
phases.pupils: Pull the line down under supervision, observe the load rise and mark arrows on the model drawing.

phases.teacher: Ask each pupil to show the two directions on a fresh model sketch and explain the change observed.
phases.pupils: Draw a downward pull arrow and an upward load arrow for the demonstrated setup.

phases.teacher: Ask what the fixed pulley changes in the observed setup.
phases.pupils: Describe the direction of the applied pull relative to the rising load.

plans.follow_up: Check pupils keep pull and load arrows distinct.

plans.label: Lesson 51
plans.title: Find pulley applications
plans.objective: Identify three uses of pulleys and explain the benefit in one case.
plans.materials: Photos of flagpoles, blinds, wells and other checked examples, scenario cards and labels.

phases.teacher: Show a flagpole rope and ask how it differs from lifting the flag directly by hand.
phases.pupils: Name one practical benefit of the pulley position.

phases.teacher: Ask groups to identify the wheel, rope and load in illustrated uses. Provide picture options with and without pulleys to compare.
phases.pupils: Find how the parts work in each use and record a practical benefit in one case.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil identifies three genuine applications and explains a benefit in one context.
phases.pupils: List three applications and connect a named benefit to the task the pulley helps perform.

phases.teacher: Ask for evidence that one chosen example really uses a pulley.
phases.pupils: Point to the wheel and rope arrangement in its image.

plans.follow_up: Revisit machines chosen simply because they lift something.

plans.label: Lesson 52
plans.title: Build and explain a pulley model
plans.objective: Raise a small test load with a working model and use a labelled sketch to explain its operation.
plans.materials: Teacher-checked pulley kits, soft cords, clamps, arrow cards and very light test loads.

phases.teacher: Show a secure model and ask what would stop the load from rising smoothly.
phases.pupils: Name one possible threading or alignment problem.

phases.teacher: Model a safe setup under teacher supervision. Check supports, allow pairs to test a very light load and ask for one adjustment if needed.
phases.pupils: Assemble the model with guidance, test one pull and revise the rope path as needed. Make a labelled sketch with motion arrows.

phases.teacher: Observe each pupil demonstrate the working model or explain the paired test. Check the drawing labels the parts and directions correctly.
phases.pupils: Raise the test load and use the wheel, rope, load and labelled arrows in an explanation.

phases.teacher: Ask which change had a visible effect on the model’s performance.
phases.pupils: Describe an adjustment and the observed result.

plans.follow_up: Recheck the safe assembly test and which arrows explain the direction change.

plans.label: Review 04
plans.title: Solar System and Machine
plans.objective: Read one orbit model and explain how changing the direction of a pull lifts a load.
plans.materials: Orbit diagram, small fixed-pulley model or diagram, arrow cards and two-question review sheet.

phases.teacher: Display an orbit drawing and a pulley drawing. Ask what travels in each.
phases.pupils: Identify the planet and the pulley load in their different models.

phases.teacher: Review the centre and motion of an orbit and demonstrate the direction of pull and load movement. Give a new diagram for each topic.
phases.pupils: Read the orbit diagram and place arrows for the demonstrated fixed pulley in pairs.

phases.teacher: Check each pupil interprets one orbit representation and correctly explains the relation of pull to load movement.
phases.pupils: Explain the orbit and add pull and load arrows with an explanation of how the fixed pulley changes direction.

phases.teacher: Ask pupils to name one useful label in each model.
phases.pupils: Name the Sun and the load or pull direction and explain what each label shows.

plans.follow_up: Recheck revolution or direction change according to the pupil’s evidence.
